title: My Card Says We Stop Being FRIENDS
premise: Everybody gets one card at eighteen that says how their closest friendship ends, and the cards are never wrong. Mine says my best friend Maya and I stop being friends at 9:14 tonight, and on the back, in tiny writing, it won't hurt. For ten years I have never been alone with her, bringing my big brother Nate to everything. Tonight is June twelfth, on a rooftop, in a suit.
twist: Nate is marrying Maya, and at 9:14 she becomes my sister: the card never said we would fight, only that we would stop being friends. Her card says the same, she worked out what it meant at eighteen and never told me, and every June twelfth she makes me read mine out loud.
world: A flat city rooftop at sunset with white folding chairs, a flower arch with a brass base, string lights and water towers on the skyline, and ten years of sunny day scenes: a mail slot hall, a parking lot, two lawns, an airport gate, a curb, a diner.
